"I am in charge of dreams. God's command is hard to follow.
If I must divine to return it,
Fear it may be too late for revival,
And I, Wū Yáng, cannot be of use."
Then descended to summon, saying:
Soul, come back! You've left your constant form,
Why wander the four directions?
Abandoning your joyful abode,
To encounter those ill omens!
Soul, come back!
The east is not to be trusted.
Giants tall as a thousand ren, seeking only souls.
Ten suns take turns, melting metal and stone.
They are used to it, but your soul would dissolve.
Come back! It cannot be trusted.
Soul, come back!
The south is not to be stayed in.
Tattooed foreheads and blackened teeth,
They use human flesh for sacrifice,
Grinding bones into paste.
Vipers swarm, giant foxes roam for miles.
Great serpents with nine heads, darting swiftly,
Devouring men to fatten their hearts.
Come back!
Do not linger long there.
Soul, come back! The west's perils,
Shifting sands for a thousand miles.
Sucked into the thunder abyss,
Scattered and unstoppable.
If lucky to escape, beyond lies barren wilderness.
Red ants like elephants, black wasps like gourds.
No grains grow,
Only thorny reeds to eat.
The soil rots the flesh,
No water to be found.
Wandering with no support,
Vast and endless.
Come back! Lest you bring harm upon yourself.
Soul, come back!
The north is not to be stayed in.
Layered ice towering high,
Flying snow for a thousand miles.
Come back!
Do not tarry long.
Soul, come back! Do not go to heaven above.
Tigers and leopards guard nine passes, pecking at those below.
A giant with nine heads, uproots trees by thousands.
Wolves with glaring eyes, prowling in packs;
They hang men for sport, casting them into deep abysses.
Only after reporting to God can one rest in peace.
Come back! Going there endangers you.
Soul, come back!
Do not descend to this netherworld.
The Earth Lord with nine twists,
His horns sharp and menacing.
Thick shoulders, bloody thumbs,
Chasing men fiercely.
Three-eyed with a tiger's head,
His body like an ox.
These all relish human flesh.
Come back!
Lest you bring disaster upon yourself.
Soul, come back! Enter the splendid gate.
The skilled summoner calls you, walking backward to lead.
Qín baskets, Qí threads, Zhèng silk netting.
Summoning tools all prepared, long calls are made.
Soul, come back! Return to your old home.
Heaven, earth, and all directions hold many treacheries.
In your chamber, images are set, tranquil and serene.
High halls and deep rooms, with tiered balustrades.
Multi-storied towers and pavilions, facing high mountains.
Latticed doors with red adornments, carved square patterns.
In winter, deep warm rooms; in summer, cool chambers.
Streams wind and return, flowing with murmurs.
Sunlit breezes sway the huì grass, orchids abound.
Through the hall to the inner room, red dust mats spread.
Polished rooms with kingfisher plumes, curved jades hung.
Kingfisher-feathered pearl quilts, radiant in unison.
Soft silk covers the walls, silk canopies drawn.
Colorful silks and fine weaves, adorned with precious jades.
The sights within the room, many rare and wondrous.
Orchid-scented candles bright, beautiful faces ready.
Sixteen maidens attend in shifts, taking turns.
Noble ladies, virtuous and graceful, numerous and swift.
Luxuriant hairdos in varied styles, filling the palace.
Their charms well-matched, surpassing generations.
Tender yet firm in resolve, truly full of intent.
With lovely face and slender form, She threads the inner chamber.
Her moth eyebrows and liquid eyes Cast glances around.
Her smooth, soft skin Reveals a loving gaze.
In the high hall and curtained alcove She waits on the prince at leisure.
Feathered canopies and kingfisher curtains Decorate the lofty hall.
Red walls and sandalwood panels, And beams of black jade.
Look up at carved rafters Painted with dragons and serpents.
Sitting in the hall, leaning on the balustrade, Facing the winding pool.
Lotus flowers begin to bloom, Mingled with water caltrops and lotus leaves.
Purple-stemmed water shield, Patterned ripples on the waves.
Guards in leopard-skin adornments Stand by the sloping banks.
Carriages with low-slung frames, Foot soldiers and cavalry arrayed.
Orchids planted by the door, Jasper trees form a hedge.
O soul, come back! Why should you go far away?
The family honors you as chief, With foods of many kinds.
Rice, millet, early wheat, Mixed with yellow millet.
Bitter, salty, sour, Hot and sweet—all are used.
Tendons of fat oxen, Stewed tender and fragrant.
Blended sour and bitter, The soup of Wú is served.
Stewed turtle and roast kid, With sugarcane sauce.
Sour wild goose and duck stew, Fried bustard and crane.
Marinated chicken and turtle meat broth, Strong-flavored yet not cloying.
Fried honey cakes and sweet pastries, With malt-sugar treats.
Jade-like wine mixed with honey, Fills the feathered cups.
Strained dregs, ice-cooled drink, Cool and refreshing vintage.
Ornate wine vessels are laid out, With jade-like nectar.
Return to your old home, Respected and free from harm.
Before the feast is fully served, The maidens of music appear.
Strike the bells, beat the drums, They perform new songs.
"Crossing the River," "Gathering Water Caltrops,"
And "Raising the Lotus" they sing.
The beauties, already drunk, Their rosy faces flushed.
With teasing glances and sidelong looks, Eyes like rippling waves.
Dressed in rich silks and fine fabrics, Elegant but not bizarre.
Long black hair and flowing tresses, Brilliant and dazzling.
Two rows of eight, identically dressed,
Begin the dance of Zhèng.
Sleeves crossing like bamboo poles,
They lower them, pressing the mats.
Reeds and zithers wildly join,
Drums thunderously beat.
The palace halls tremble and shake,
As "The Stirring Chǔ" resounds.
Songs of Wú and ballads of Cài,
Played in the Dàlǚ mode.
Men and women sit mingled, Disordered and indistinguishable.
Belts and hat-strings cast aside, Strewn in confusion.
Seductive entertainers from Zhèng and Wèi Come to mingle among them.
The finale of "The Stirring Chǔ" Stands out uniquely.
Ivory pieces and bamboo chips, For the game of Liùbó.
Partners advance together, Urgently pressing each other.
Making "owl" and "seizing" moves, They shout for "five white."
Jìn-made rhino horn dice, Cost the light of day.
Bells clang, stands shake, And catalpa zithers are plucked.
Drinking pleasure never ceases, Sinking day and night.
Orchid-scented candles brightly burn, Ornate lamps intricately set.
Composing with deepest thought, Borrowing orchid's fragrance.
Each person has their utmost, Chanting in shared heart.
Drinking vintage, enjoying to the full, Delighting ancestors past.
O soul, come back! Return to your old home.
Epilogue:
As the new year opens in spring, I haste southward,
Green duckweed spreads its leaves, white angelica grows.
My road passes through Lújiāng, to the left long marshes,
Leaning by pools and fields, gazing far and wide.
Black steeds in teams of four, a thousand chariots aligned,
Torches raised high blaze, dark faces glowing.
On foot or at gallop, leading the charge,
Reining in swiftly, guiding the chariot rightward.
Racing with the king to Mèng, competing who's first.
The king himself shot, startling the blue rhinoceros.
Red dawn follows night, time cannot linger.
Orchids cover the path, this road grows faint.
Deep, deep the river waters, above them maples stand,
Eyes straining over a thousand miles, spring heart grieves.
O soul, come back! Lament for Jiāngnán!
Youth receives the farewell, bright the sun shines.
Spring energy bursts forth, all things hasten.
Dark spirits roam everywhere, soul has no escape.
O soul, return! Do not wander far.
O soul, come back!
Go not east,
Go not west, nor south, nor north.
In the east lies the great sea,
Drowning waters deep and vast.
Hornless dragons swim together,
Rising and falling endlessly.
Mist and rain fall ceaselessly,
White and gleaming, clinging.
O soul, go not east!
The Valley of Sun is silent.
O soul, go not south!
South has fiery flames for a thousand miles,
Vipers slithering long.
Mountains and forests perilous and narrow,
Tigers and leopards coiling.
Yúyōng fish and short foxes,
Great serpents lifting high.
O soul, go not south!
The sand-shooter wounds the body.
O soul, go not west!
Western lands of flowing sands,
Vast and boundless, expansive.
Heads like pigs, eyes protruding,
Hair disheveled, wild.
Long claws and jagged teeth,
Laughing madly, deranged.
O soul, go not west!
Full of harm and injury.
O soul, go not north!
North has cold mountains,
Chuòlóng dragons crimson red.
Dài River cannot be crossed,
Depth immeasurable.
Sky white and brilliant,
Cold congealing. O soul, go not there!
The North Pole overflows.
O soul, return!
To leisure and tranquility.
Indulge in Jīng and Chǔ,
Secure and settled.
Fulfill ambitions and desires,
Heart and mind at peace.
Lifelong eternal joy,
Years and longevity extended.
O soul, come back!
Joy beyond words.
Five grains six ren high,
Set with wild rice stems.
Cauldrons simmer full in view,
Blended to fragrant perfection.
Inside, crane, dove, and swan,
Seasoned with jackal soup.
O soul, come back!
Feast on what you will.
Fresh turtle and sweet chicken,
Blended with Chǔ cheese.
Minced pork and bitter dog,
Sliced with pickled herbs.
Wú sour with artemisia,
Not too strong or weak.
O soul, come back!
Choose as you please.
Roast crow and steamed duck,
Quail stew set forth.
Fried bream and sparrow broth,
Swiftly refreshing to taste.
O soul, come back!
Feast first on delicacies.
Fourfold vintage fully ripe,
Not harsh to the throat.
Clear fragrance, chilled to drink,
Not for servants to guzzle.
Wú sweet liquor with white yeast,
Mixed with Chǔ clear wine.
O soul, come back!
No need for haste or fear.
Music of Dài, Qín, Zhèng, Wèi,
Sounding reeds and strings.
Fúxī's "Jià Biàn,"
Chǔ's "Láo Shāng."
Songs harmonize with "Yáng Ā,"
Zhào flutes lead.
O soul, come back!
Set the kōngsāng zither.
Two rows of eight dance in turn,
Chanting poems and rhapsodies.
Strike bells, tune chimes,
Entertainers perform in finale.
Four modes compete in spirit,
Reaching sound's extremes.
O soul, come back!
Listen to songs composed.
Vermilion lips, gleaming teeth,
Lovely and beautiful.
Virtuous and composed by nature,
Accustomed to elegance.
Plump flesh, fine bones,
Graceful and pleasing.
O soul, come back!
At ease and comfortable.
Lovely eyes suited for smiling,
Delicate moth eyebrows.
Features refined and elegant,
Youthful rosy face.
O soul, come back!
Peaceful and serene.
Graceful and ample,
Beautiful and fine.
Full cheeks, ears close-set,
Curved brows like compass-drawn.
Generous heart, graceful manner,
Loveliness displayed.
Slender waist, fair neck,
Like the Xiānbī people.
Your fame is like the sun, shining over the four seas.
Your virtue matches heaven's, governing all the people.
Northward reaching Yōulíng, southward to Jiāozhǐ.
Westward bordering Yángcháng, eastward to the farthest sea.
O soul, come back! Honor the worthy and scholars.
Issue policies and promote good deeds, prohibit harshness and tyranny.
Elevate the outstanding to high positions, punish slanderers and the incompetent.
With the upright and capable in office, they draw near to Yǔ's command.
Heroes and talents hold power, spreading benefits far and wide.
O soul, come back! For the sake of the state and family.
Majestic and illustrious, the virtue of heaven shines bright.
The three dukes dignified, ascending and descending the hall.
All feudal lords gather, appointing the nine ministers.
The clear targets set, the great archery target stretched.
Bows in hand, arrows at the ready, they bow and defer with courtesy.
O soul, come back! Honor the three ancient kings.
